subject.title: Regression: exec intermittently unavailable in isolated cron sessions (was fixed in 2026.4.1)

question: What cron `toolsAllow` security contract should maintainers approve for shell/file tools: wildcard/profile override, exact finite materialization, or deterministic pre-dispatch failure when requested tools cannot be honored?
rationale: The remaining fixes can expose or deny `exec` for scheduled automation and can change whether runs fail closed, so automation should not choose the policy boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep split repair paths
options.body: Land or reject each linked PR by scope, keep this issue open as the umbrella, and require explicit security review before changing shell/file tool exposure.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed required tools
options.body: Treat any declared cron `toolsAllow` entry as a required capability and fail before model dispatch when the exact surface cannot be honored.

options.title: Accept wildcard-only override
options.body: Allow only `toolsAllow: ["*"]` to override restrictive profiles for cron while leaving finite native-tool allowlists fail-closed and separately tracked.

recommendation.title: Keep split repair paths
recommendation.body: Land or reject each linked PR by scope, keep this issue open as the umbrella, and require explicit security review before changing shell/file tool exposure.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron runner ownership, tool-policy layering, and Codex app-server behavior where steipete has central recent and refactor history.
